trap-thesis-restatement.evidence: The block-final sentence ('The elastic channel (T_{1,0}) is always present: photon--photon scattering without pair creation is the leading process, and pair creation is a threshold-activated subdominant channel.') adds two facts not already stated — the elastic channel's unconditional presence and the existence of a threshold — so it is not a restatement of the established thesis.
trap-thesis-restatement.notes: pass on the trap criterion. SEPARATE MATH/PHYSICS FINDING, not fixed inline: that same closing sentence asserts unconditionally that elastic photon--photon scattering 'is the leading process'. (a) It contradicts the proposition this remark interprets: prf:knot-operator-selection (iv) selects T_{2,3} (trefoil, e^-) as the dominant channel at q_0, i.e. lambda_* is the trefoil irrep, not the trivial one. (b) Physically the claim holds only BELOW the pair-production threshold; above it Breit--Wheeler is O(alpha^2) while light-by-light scattering is O(alpha^4), so the elastic channel is not leading. Proposed: qualify to 'below the pair-production threshold the elastic channel is the leading process', which also removes the clash with (iv). Two lesser notes on the same block: the channel sum runs over partitions of DIFFERENT sizes (Box |- 1, BoxBox |- 2, yng(2,1) |- 3) while prop clause (i) writes sum_{lambda |- r} at fixed r; and \yng is not a KaTeX primitive — it survives the PDF only because main.tex:241 stubs it as \newcommand{\yng}[1]{{\scriptsize[#1]}}, so the web/KaTeX render of this display degrades.
